elements.element: No liquidated damages payable by Customer
elements.evidence: "Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages"
"or penalty for each week the invoice remains unpaid"

elements.element: Early-termination fee expressly capped at 3 months' fees
elements.evidence: Redline contains no early-termination fee provision; only "Customer shall not be liable to Vendor for any liquidated damages or penalty"

elements.element: That capped early-termination fee is the sole liquidated amount
elements.evidence: No sole-liquidated-amount language anywhere in clause 7.7 as redlined

reasons: Preferred position is fully achieved: the 15% weekly liquidated damages charge is replaced with an express statement that Customer owes no liquidated damages or penalty.

The edit is confined to the operative payment obligation in 7.7; the trigger language and the balance of Section 7 (including ordinary late-payment interest) are untouched, so no unrelated commercial term is impaired.
Fallback is not satisfied and need not be, since the drafter's locked target is preferred and the two levels are separate bargains.

Note only: the retained residue "If any invoice is not paid within ten days of its due date" and "for each week the invoice remains unpaid" leaves a slightly awkward, narrower-than-necessary framing (it reads as a no-liability statement limited to that trigger); this operates against Customer's own breadth rather than adding Vendor protection, so it is not an extra-words minimality failure, but a clean deletion of the charge would have read better.
